name: World Trade Center North Tower (1 WTC)
coordSource: Wikipedia coordinates for the tower (1 World Trade Center (1970-2001)); the footprint is now the North Pool of the 9/11 Memorial
cause: September 11 attacks: hit by American Airlines Flight 11, collapsed 10:28 a.m.
notes: Height 417 m = CTBUH architectural top (roof); antenna tip 526.7 m not counted. Completion 1972 per CTBUH; first tenants Dec 1970, topped out Dec 1970. replacedBy is the successor tower on the same WTC site, NOT the same footprint: One World Trade Center stands about 100 m north-west of the old North Tower, whose footprint is now the memorial's North Pool. Debris removal ended May 2002.

name: World Trade Center South Tower (2 WTC)
coordSource: Wikipedia coordinates for the tower (2 World Trade Center (1971-2001)); the footprint is now the South Pool of the 9/11 Memorial
cause: September 11 attacks: hit by United Airlines Flight 175, collapsed 9:59 a.m.
notes: Height 415.1 m = CTBUH architectural top. Completion 1973 per CTBUH; tenants from January 1972, topped out July 1971. No tower stands on its footprint (memorial South Pool). The new '2 World Trade Center' in the dataset (id 50966, under construction) carries the name but sits on a different plot on Church Street, so it is not given as replacedBy.

name: AXA Tower
coordSource: Singapore OneMap address point for 8 Shenton Way (now The Skywaters); Wikipedia gives 1.2758,103.8472 (about 10 m away)
cause: Demolished for Skywaters Residences (8 Shenton Way redevelopment)
notes: Closed May 2022; demolition began shortly after (Wikipedia) and CTBUH records it as demolished in 2023. Tallest building ever voluntarily demolished. replacedBy (dataset id 44843, ~300 m) is still under construction (due 2028).

name: Union Carbide Building (270 Park Avenue)
coordSource: Derived: Wikipedia says the 52-storey slab stood on the Park Avenue side of the block, set back ~33-50 ft from the Park Avenue lot line; point placed accordingly using the NYC footprint polygon of the new tower on the same block. Wikipedia's own coordinate (40.75583,-73.97556) is ~9 m away.
cause: Replaced by the new JPMorganChase headquarters at 270 Park Avenue
notes: Demolition permit January 2019, demolition 2019-2021 (Wikipedia); CTBUH lists the demolition year as 2020. Completed mid-2021. Tallest building ever voluntarily demolished until AXA Tower. A 13-storey annex on the Madison Avenue side came down too.

name: Singer Building
coordSource: Derived: the tower stood at the north-west corner of Broadway and Liberty Street, set back 30 ft from Broadway (Wikipedia); point placed from the corner of the One Liberty Plaza footprint (NYC open data). Wikipedia's coordinate 40.70972,-74.01083 is ~18 m away.
cause: Replaced by One Liberty Plaza (U.S. Steel Building)
notes: 186.6 m = CTBUH architectural height (612 ft roof); tip 204-205 m. 41 storeys (sometimes quoted as 47, which counts the dome and lantern). Demolition had begun by September 1967; CTBUH gives 1968 as the demolition year; last scrap removed early 1969. World's tallest building 1908-1909.

name: 7 World Trade Center (1987)
coordSource: Derived: the 1987 building ran ~100 m west from West Broadway between Barclay and Vesey streets (Wikipedia); point placed ~50 m west of the West Broadway building line using the NYC building-footprint polygon of today's 7 WTC. Uncertainty about +/-20 m. Wikipedia gives 40.7133,-74.0119 (east end of the old footprint).
cause: Collapsed on September 11, 2001 after fires started by debris from the North Tower
notes: Height 185.9 m (610 ft) is the roof height given by Wikipedia/NIST; CTBUH lists only 173.7 m (570 ft). Either way it is over 150 m. The 2006 7 WTC (dataset id 1117) occupies the eastern part of the old footprint; Greenwich Street was reopened through the western part.

name: CPF Building
coordSource: Singapore OneMap address point for 79 Robinson Road (CapitaSky, built on the same plot); the dataset's coordinate for 79 Robinson Road is 16 m away. Wikipedia's CPF coordinate (1.276833,103.847861) is ~40 m off.
notes: Floors: 45 per CTBUH, 46 per Wikipedia. Last tenant left 20 Feb 2017; demolished 2017 (Wikipedia) and CTBUH gives 2018 as demolition year.

name: Toshiba Building
coordSource: CTBUH coordinate as carried in the site's dataset (id 2949)
cause: Being taken down for the Shibaura Project; BLUE FRONT SHIBAURA Tower N (~227-235 m) to be built on the site
notes: ALREADY IN THE DATASET as a standing tower (id 2949, 'Toshiba Building', Completed 1984, 167 m) - that row should be retired/flagged to avoid a duplicate. Demolition by Shimizu started 1 Oct 2025 and is scheduled to finish late April 2028 (Kensetsu News, 2 Sep 2025; photos of demolition May 2026). It was still partly standing in mid-2026, so 'gone' = year demolition began per the brief. Japanese sources give 165.95 m; 167 m is CTBUH's figure. Toshiba moved out 1 Aug 2025. Tower N is not in the dataset; Tower S next door is (id 50356).

name: Fuji Xerox Towers
coordSource: Singapore OneMap address point for 80 Anson Road (Newport Plaza, under construction on the same plot); Wikipedia gives 1°16'24"N 103°50'38"E (~25 m away)
cause: Replaced by Newport Plaza / Newport Residences (City Developments Ltd)
notes: Height 164.9 m per CTBUH (165 m per Wikipedia and The Straits Times). Floors 40 per CTBUH, 38 per Wikipedia. Demolition began in the second half of 2021; part of the remaining structure collapsed during demolition on 15 June 2023, killing a worker; CTBUH/Wikipedia list 2023 as the demolition year. The replacement (Newport Plaza) is not in the dataset.

name: Morrison Hotel
coordSource: Estimated from the hotel's address (15-29 S. Clark St, east side of Clark just south of Madison; US Census geocoder places 21 S. Clark at 41.88192,-87.63080) and accounts that the 1925 tower faced Clark Street. Uncertainty about +/-30 m. Wikipedia's coordinate 41.8816,-87.6301 is the centre of today's Chase Tower block, ~40 m east.
cause: Replaced by the First National Bank Building (now Chase Tower)
notes: 160.3 m (526 ft) per CTBUH; earlier CTBUH list said 159.7 m. 45 floors (CTBUH/Wikipedia infobox; some texts say 46). The hotel grew in stages (1915, 1918, 1925 tower, 1930s); the 1925 tower is the 150 m+ part. Sources give only the year 1965 for demolition.

name: World Trade Center Building (Tokyo)
formerNames: 世界貿易センタービルディング
coordSource: Wikipedia (EN and JA) coordinates for the building
cause: Hamamatsucho 2-chome redevelopment; new World Trade Center Main/North Tower (235 m) being built on the site
notes: Heights differ by source: 158 m (CTBUH architectural, used here), 162.6 m roof (English Wikipedia), 152 m (top floor; most Japanese sources). All are over 150 m. Closed 30 June 2021; demolition August 2021 to March 2023 (Japanese Wikipedia). CTBUH still shows it as 'Completed' (out of date). The new tower on the site (WTC North/Main Tower, due 2027) is not in the dataset; the dataset's 'World Trade Center South Tower' (id 36120) is on the adjacent plot, not the old site.

name: Deutsche Bank Building
coordSource: Wikipedia coordinates; cross-checked with NYC PLUTO lot centroids for the site's block (block centroid 40.70985,-74.01330, ~15 m away)
cause: Badly damaged and contaminated in the September 11 attacks; dismantled floor by floor
notes: 157.6 m per CTBUH (earlier CTBUH list 157.9 m; Wikipedia says 163 m roof). Stood damaged and empty from 2001; deconstruction began March 2007 (delayed by a fatal fire in Aug 2007) and was finished January-February 2011. If the map should hide it from 2001, use 2001 instead of 2007. Site now holds Liberty Park / Vehicular Security Center and St. Nicholas shrine; 5 World Trade Center is planned (paused 2026) and is not in the dataset.

name: UIC Building
coordSource: Wikipedia coordinates for the old building; Singapore OneMap's point for 5 Shenton Way is ~22 m away
notes: Borderline-ish at 152 m (CTBUH 152 m / 499 ft). Completion 1974 per CTBUH, 1973 per Wikipedia and The Straits Times. Demolition started about July 2012 (part of the car-park block collapsed on Thursday 2 Aug 2012, a month into demolition) and finished in 2013.

name: One Meridian Plaza
coordSource: CTBUH coordinate of The Residences at the Ritz-Carlton (dataset id 3454), which was built on the One Meridian Plaza site at 15th St & South Penn Square; Wikipedia gives 39.95139,-75.16472 (~29 m away)
cause: Gutted by the February 1991 fire that killed three firefighters; empty for years, then dismantled
notes: BORDERLINE: exactly 150.0 m (492 ft) per CTBUH and Wikipedia. Stood fire-damaged and vacant 1991-1998 (use 1991 instead if the map should drop it when it went out of use). Demolition started third week of July 1998 and finished by Christmas 1999 (Philly YIMBY). Part of the site also holds the W/Element Philadelphia hotel (dataset id 2054).

name: Menara Tun Razak
coordSource: Average of two independent web points for the site on Jalan Raja Laut (penang-traveltips GPS 3.15281,101.69505; SkyscraperPage map link 3.152893,101.695038). Not verified against imagery; uncertainty maybe +/-30 m.
cause: Taken down during Tradewinds Corp's redevelopment of the site (details disputed)
notes: LEAST CERTAIN ENTRY. Height exactly 150 m (CTBUH and Wikipedia) - borderline. Completion 1981 per CTBUH, 1983 per Wikipedia; 37 floors per CTBUH, 35 per Wikipedia. CTBUH (building page and its 2018 'Tallest Demolished Buildings' study, rank 7) and Wikipedia say demolished in 2014. But owner Tradewinds announced in 2010-2012 that it would REFURBISH the tower and build a second one beside it; a 15 Jan 2014 fire on floors 27-30 happened during what the Malaysian safety department called renovation work; and a SkyscraperCity thread is titled 'Menara Tun Razak 2 & refurbished Menara Tun Razak 1 (50 fl & 26 fl)'. Exact demolition dates not found. Worth checking satellite/street imagery before relying on it.
